hook: FBI Photo B14 is a monochrome still image captured by a U.S. military system in 2025, showing two small dark circular objects near the center of the frame with a crosshair overlay, submitted to AARO after redaction with no accompanying mission report.
why_it_matters: This image represents a direct FBI submission to AARO under the post-2022 mandatory reporting framework, but its evidentiary value is undermined by three compounding factors: redactions applied before AARO received it, absence of a mission report, and a corrupted system timestamp. The operator's documented inability to identify the objects makes this a genuine unresolved case rather than a misidentification closeout. The pre-submission redaction is notable — it means AARO received an already-degraded version of a military sensor record.

key_findings.finding: Two small dark circular objects were observed near the center of the frame in imagery from a U.S. military system, and the operator was unable to positively identify them.
The original imagery was redacted before submission to AARO, and no accompanying mission report was provided, leaving the operational context unknown.
The system date and time were not correctly set, rendering the embedded timestamp in the image unreliable for establishing when the observation occurred.
A digital artifact or distortion is visible along the edge of the redaction box in the lower right quadrant, indicating post-capture image manipulation prior to submission.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The document was submitted directly to AARO by the FBI as part of the formal UAP reporting pipeline, making AARO the primary institutional recipient and analytical body for this record.

The imagery originates from an unspecified U.S. military system, which could fall under Air Force sensor infrastructure historically associated with Wright-Patterson, though no direct connection is stated.
